#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(list_path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    quarantined = quarantined_files(entries)

    paths = argv if argv else [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin if ln.strip()]
    kept = []
    for p in paths:
        norm = p.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if norm in quarantined:
            entry = next(e for e in entries if e["file"] == norm)
            print(f"::warning::quarantined (gh-1199 AC6), skipping {norm} — "
                  f"{entry.get('issue', 'no issue link')}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    for p in kept:
        print(p)
    if not kept:
        print("::warning::quarantine removed every target — the shard runs "
              "nothing this round", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]

            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [pty-integration-linux]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1

# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run

name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(list_path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    quarantined = quarantined_files(entries)

    paths = argv if argv else [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin if ln.strip()]
    kept = []
    for p in paths:
        norm = p.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if norm in quarantined:
            entry = next(e for e in entries if e["file"] == norm)
            print(f"::warning::quarantined (gh-1199 AC6), skipping {norm} — "
                  f"{entry.get('issue', 'no issue link')}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    for p in kept:
        print(p)
    if not kept:
        print("::warning::quarantine removed every target — the shard runs "
              "nothing this round", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(list_path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    quarantined = quarantined_files(entries)

    paths = argv if argv else [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin if ln.strip()]
    kept = []
    for p in paths:
        norm = p.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if norm in quarantined:
            entry = next(e for e in entries if e["file"] == norm)
            print(f"::warning::quarantined (gh-1199 AC6), skipping {norm} — "
                  f"{entry.get('issue', 'no issue link')}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    for p in kept:
        print(p)
    if not kept:
        print("::warning::quarantine removed every target — the shard runs "
              "nothing this round", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm

      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration
          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Issue #943 (vector 3): one warm fa boot before the PTY shards. The
      # first `dart` invocation pays the native-assets build hooks (20-30 s
      # under load) — paid HERE instead of inside a test's boot timeout
      # (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5 on 2026-09-24). Both invocation shapes
      # the tests use (file path + `dart run`) are warmed; every shard of
      # this matrix job does it, so each shard process meets a warm cache
      # and the duration gate below measures warm-boot truth.
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

  # Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [pty-integration-linux]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(list_path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    quarantined = quarantined_files(entries)

    paths = argv if argv else [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin if ln.strip()]
    kept = []
    for p in paths:
        norm = p.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if norm in quarantined:
            entry = next(e for e in entries if e["file"] == norm)
            print(f"::warning::quarantined (gh-1199 AC6), skipping {norm} — "
                  f"{entry.get('issue', 'no issue link')}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    for p in kept:
        print(p)
    if not kept:
        print("::warning::quarantine removed every target — the shard runs "
              "nothing this round", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(list_path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    quarantined = quarantined_files(entries)

    paths = argv if argv else [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin if ln.strip()]
    kept = []
    for p in paths:
        norm = p.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if norm in quarantined:
            entry = next(e for e in entries if e["file"] == norm)
            print(f"::warning::quarantined (gh-1199 AC6), skipping {norm} — "
                  f"{entry.get('issue', 'no issue link')}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    for p in kept:
        print(p)
    if not kept:
        print("::warning::quarantine removed every target — the shard runs "
              "nothing this round", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0

          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"

      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.

          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14

        with:

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk.       # under load) — paid HERE instead of inside a test's boot timeout
      # (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5 on 2026-09-24). Both invocation shapes
      # the tests use (file path + `dart run`) are warmed; every shard of
      # this matrix job does it, so each shard process meets a warm cache
      # and the duration gate below measures warm-boot truth.
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null

          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined

          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)

          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(list_path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    quarantined = quarantined_files(entries)

    paths = argv if argv else [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin if ln.strip()]
    kept = []
    for p in paths:
        norm = p.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if norm in quarantined:
            entry = next(e for e in entries if e["file"] == norm)
            print(f"::warning::quarantined (gh-1199 AC6), skipping {norm} — "
                  f"{entry.get('issue', 'no issue link')}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    for p in kept:
        print(p)
    if not kept:
        print("::warning::quarantine removed every target — the shard runs "
              "nothing this round", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the gh-1199 AC6 flake quarantine to a set of test targets.

Reads candidate test paths (one per line) from stdin, or as positional
arguments, and prints the paths that STAY in the gate to stdout. Files
listed in scripts/test_quarantine.json are dropped — with a `::warning::`
per skip, so the gate log always shows what the quarantine is shielding
(E3: a quarantine must never swallow a real regression silently).

Usage (the CI legs pipe their shard selection through it):

    python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json 0 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    find test/integration -name '*_test.dart' \
      | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py

    python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check
        validates the quarantine list itself: entries must reference
        existing files that are tagged `integration` and carry an issue
        link — a stale or under-documented entry fails the static gate.

The list is checked in and reviewed in the fix PR; flake_watch.py
(auto-filed flake issues) proposes entries with the proving runs attached.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a malformed list or --check failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag

LIST_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                         "test_quarantine.json")

REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("file", "issue", "since", "runs")


def load_quarantine(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> list:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        doc = json.load(f)
    entries = doc.get("quarantined")
    if not isinstance(entries, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: 'quarantined' must be a list")
    return entries


def quarantined_files(entries: list) -> set:
    return {e["file"] for e in entries}


def check(path: str = LIST_PATH) -> int:
    """Validate the list; a stale/under-documented entry fails the gate."""
    ok = True
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(path)

entries = load_quarantine(path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("file", "<missing file>")
        for field in REQUIRED_FIELDS:
            if not e.get(field):
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: missing '{field}' "
                      f"(every entry needs {list(REQUIRED_FIELDS)})",
                      file=sys.stderr)
        file = e.get("file")
        if file and not os.path.isfile(file):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file does not exist — "
                  f"remove the entry (fix landed) or fix the path",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        elif file and not file_has_tag(file, "integration"):
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: file is not tagged "
                  f"'integration' — the quarantine only shields the "
                  f"integration gate legs", file=sys.stderr)
        runs = e.get("runs") or []
        if runs and len({str(r) for r in runs}) < 2:
            ok = False
            print(f"::error::quarantine entry {name}: 'runs' must carry the "
                  f">=2 distinct proving gate runs (gh-1199 AC6/E3)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
    print(f"Quarantine list OK: {len(entries)} entr(ies), all documented")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv == ["--check"]:
        return check()
    list_path = LIST_PATH
    if "--list" in argv:
        i = argv.index("--list")
        try:
            list_path = argv[i + 1]
        except IndexError:
            print("ERROR: --list needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        del argv[i:i + 2]
    try:
        entries = load_quarantine(list_path)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    quarantined = quarantined_files(entries)

    paths = argv if argv else [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin if ln.strip()]
    kept = []
    for p in paths:
        norm = p.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if norm in quarantined:
            entry = next(e for e in entries if e["file"] == norm)
            print(f"::warning::quarantined (gh-1199 AC6), skipping {norm} — "
                  f"{entry.get('issue', 'no issue link')}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    for p in kept:
        print(p)
    if not kept:
        print("::warning::quarantine removed every target — the shard runs "
              "nothing this round", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
